messages:
sasha: Heads up — after enabling LL128 + proto selector on staging (8x A100) we saw a 15-25% throughput drop for small-batch chat workloads. p99 up ~30ms. Job: job/ci-perf-2101, traces attached.

infra-bot: perf-job job/ci-perf-2101 finished — artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/2101/artifacts :white_check_mark:

matt: Can you paste the nvprof/trace snippet and the exact NCCL envs you used? Did we flip the kernel selector recently? @sasha

sasha: Repro envs we used: 
```
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=4
NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=proto_prefer_ll128
```
Trace (summary):
```
Allreduce(total):  6.2ms -> 8.1ms (avg per op)
CUDA kernel memcpy_h2d: 0.3ms
ncclKernel_LL128_step: 4.8ms (dominant)
KV cache prefetch: 0.9ms
```

liam: Hmm looks like small-message allreduces got worse with LL128. Did channels get auto-enabled? LL128 is great for large messages but channels + LL128 sometimes serializes tiny fragments. Try toggling NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1 or NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE to confirm. Also try NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=16384 (if supported) to force SIMPLE under threshold.

rachel: Another vector — batching heuristics changed recently so average tokens per batch dropped ~20%, causing smaller allreduce payloads. KV cache prefetches also increased number of in-flight small tensors. That combo pushes us into pessimistic kernel choices.

sasha: Quick repro command I ran locally: 
```bash
export NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=4
./bin/chat_infer --model t5x --gpu 8 --batch-size 4 --seq-len 512 --profile
```
Result: throughput 920 reqs/s (baseline with NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE was ~1150 reqs/s).

matt: Can you run nccl-tests microbench for small message sizes and vary channels? E.g.
```bash
mpirun -np 8 ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 65536 -f 2 -g 1 --iters 100
# vary NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1,2,4 and NCCL_PROTO=LL128,SIMPLE
```
Would like to see latency curve for 128B..64KB.

liam: Also attach pprof flame graph for the runtime when running the microbench — show host vs device time and show nccl ops stacked. If LL128 kernel shows serialization then channel mapping heuristic might be suboptimal.

sasha: Ran the microbench quick sweep (8 GPUs):
```
128B: SIMPLE 0.12ms, LL128 0.25ms
4KB: SIMPLE 0.45ms, LL128 0.6ms
64KB: SIMPLE 2.4ms,   LL128 1.9ms
```
So LL128 helps large msgs but hurts <32KB. Matches the regression.

rachel: Recommendation: adjust runtime kernel selector to prefer SIMPLE for median message size < 32KB or when average tokens/batch < 800. Also add a runtime override flag for NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS per-workload. I'll open a tiny PR to expose `runtime.nccL.override_small_msg_proto` and a perf test.

sasha: Sounds good — I'll run a sweep across our chat suite with NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1 and proto=SIMPLE and post CI numbers later today. Thanks for the quick triage :eyes:.
